title: What’s the spookiest theatre show you’ve ever seen? #theatre #hallowe...
transcript: here are the spookiest theatre shows I've ever attended and I'm not talking about Beetlejuice or Little Shop of horrors or Sweeney Todd I'm talking about shows that actually sent chills down my spine and gave me that shot of frightened adrenaline an obvious one is The Woman in black which I saw during its 34 year run in the West End but it also played New York a couple times and granted the play is kind of silly at times but it's probably the closest thing I've seen to like a pure straight up horror experience in theatre where like it's not just the iconography of the horror genre it's actually designed to be scary next I have Grey House which I think a lot of people expected to be more scary than it was given this marketing especially but I still think it was extremely creepy and there were a couple solid jump scares in there as well similarly the stage adaptation of the vampire movie Let The Right One In was in a lot of ways more absorbing and wistful than it was outright scary but there was still an unsettling eeriness throughout the show and at least one very memorable jump scare then there's Viola's room which is still running in New York for the next couple weeks, incidentally I saw this one in London and I found it pretty exhilarating and there were times especially toward the end where I was genuinely kind of freaked out by the story The Weir by Connor McPherson is more about ghost stories and what purpose they serve for communities and for individuals but when we get into the ghost story sections I did find it pretty haunting finally I have one that probably not as many people have heard of which is The Thin Place by Lucas Hnath it's about a woman who goes to a psychic to try to communicate with her late grandmother and her missing mother most of the play is not very spooky but there is one sequence at the end where they go into her abandoned childhood home that is basically as tense and chillingly creepy as anything I've seen in like a ghosty horror movie but what are some of the scariest shows you've ever seen on stage? happy Halloween everyone!
classificationReason: Lists 4+ 'spookiest' shows the creator has attended (The Woman in Black, Grey House, Let the Right One In, Viola's Room); no single show is the primary focus.
